problem.title: 1M+ Concurrent Timer Wheel Scheduler

spark.summary: Design a lock-minimal timeout scheduler for 1,000,000 concurrent connections with 200k cancels/sec.
spark.keyTakeaway: When nodes partition or reboot past retry windows, use doubly-linked timing-wheel buckets with DelayQueue-driven tick advancement to avoid idle polling.
spark.byteSummary: A naive min-heap saturates on 200k timer mutations/sec. Combining a hierarchical timing wheel with a DelayQueue over non-empty buckets avoids empty-tick CPU spinning while preserving O(1) insert and O(1) cancel.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement 1M+ Concurrent Timer Wheel Scheduler without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When nodes partition or reboot past retry windows, use doubly-linked timing-wheel buckets with DelayQueue-driven tick advancement to avoid idle polling.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When 1M+ Concurrent Timer Wheel Scheduler experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.
